subject: economics
title: Sectoral Aspects of Indian Economy
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or complete the table).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai and Kolkata are ______ cities. (b) Towns and cities are ______ areas.
questions.answer:
(a) metro
(b) urban

questions.q: Give one word: (a) Building roads, bridges and dams. (b) Raising crops on fields.
questions.answer:
(a) Construction.
(b) Agriculture (cultivation).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The ______ sector pays more than the agricultural sector. (b) Agriculture belongs to the ______ sector.
questions.answer:
(a) service (tertiary)
(b) primary

questions.q: State True or False: (a) Agriculture still gives more employment than services. (b) A small-scale industry needs at least ₹25 lakh of spending on plant and machinery.
questions.answer:
(a) True — about 50% of workers are in agriculture.
(b) True (as per the NIOS text).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Self-employed people work in their own ______. (b) Nation-building is possible because of ______-scale industries.
questions.answer:
(a) business (small business)
(b) small

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Crops give food and ______ items. (b) Manufacturing belongs to the ______ sector.
questions.answer:
(a) non-food
(b) secondary

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name the sub-sectors of the primary sector.
questions.answer: (1) Agriculture and allied activities (livestock, poultry, dairy), (2) fishery, (3) forestry, (4) mining and quarrying.

questions.q: Name the production units in the secondary sector.
questions.answer: Manufacturing units — small (shoes, textiles, printing, furniture) and large (steel, automobiles, aluminium) — construction units, and gas, water and electricity supply units.

questions.q: What is the share of the primary sector in national income?
questions.answer: Agriculture contributed more than 50% of national income at independence. Its share fell to about 15% in 2009–10 as industry and services grew.

or.answer: Activities in urban areas other than farming: manufacturing, construction, and gas, water and electricity supply (secondary), and trade, transport, banking and other services (tertiary).

questions.q: State two characteristics of a small-scale industry.
questions.answer:
(1) It can be set up with a minimum of ₹25 lakh spent on plant and machinery.
(2) It mostly uses labour-intensive technology, giving many jobs — about 3.12 crore.

questions.q: Explain manufacturing in the secondary sector.
questions.answer: Manufacturing turns raw materials into goods in factories. It may be small-scale (shoes, textiles, glass, furniture) or large-scale (steel, automobiles, aluminium), and employs skilled workers.

or.answer: Food is the most basic need, and agriculture produces it — about 234 million tonnes of food grains in 2008–09 — for India's large and growing population.

questions.q: Why does the primary sector employ the largest section of the population?
questions.answer: Agriculture is India's traditional occupation in villages. About 70% of people depended on it at independence and about 50% still work in it, because other jobs have grown slowly.

questions.q: How do rural people earn a living?
questions.answer: Through agriculture and allied activities (crops, livestock, poultry, dairy), forestry (timber, firewood, herbs), fishery and mining.

or.answer: Timber, firewood, herbal medicines, bamboo and grass (for paper).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of the tertiary sector in the Indian economy.
questions.answer:
(1) It contributes the largest share of national income — 55.2% in 2009–10.
(2) It employs 29.4% of workers and pays more than agriculture.
(3) It attracts foreign direct investment in banking, insurance, trade, hotels and IT.
(4) It earns foreign exchange through service exports such as IT and consultancy.

questions.q: Explain the importance of the primary sector.
questions.answer:
(1) It produces food for millions — about 234 million tonnes of food grains.
(2) It is the largest employer (about 50% of workers).
(3) It provides raw materials to the sugar, jute, cotton textile, paper and food-processing industries.
(4) It still contributes a share of national income (about 15%).

questions.q: 'The primary sector provides raw materials to industries.' Explain.
questions.answer:
Many industries depend on agriculture.
Sugar mills need sugarcane, jute mills need jute, textile mills need cotton, and vanaspati needs oilseeds.
Paper needs grass and bamboo.
The food-processing industry (pickles, jam, juice, biscuits) runs on farm produce.

questions.q: How are agriculture, industry and services linked?
questions.answer:
Industry supplies agriculture with pumps, fertiliser, pesticides and tractors.
Agriculture supplies food and raw materials to industry.
Services — transport, communication, banking and trade — carry goods and money between them. A farmer buys a pump through a shop, pays by money that reaches the factory through a bank, and the truck carries food back to the town.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the production activities of the secondary sector and its role in the economy.
questions.answer:
Activities: (1) manufacturing — small-scale (shoes, textiles, furniture) and large-scale (steel, automobiles); (2) construction — buildings, roads, bridges, dams; (3) gas, water and electricity supply.
Role: (1) its share of national income rose from 14% at independence to 28% in 2009–10; (2) it employs about 3.3 crore people; (3) it builds infrastructure — roads, railways, dams such as Hirakud and Bhakra-Nangal, towers; (4) it supplies consumer goods such as clothes, soap, cycles and cars.

questions.q: Explain the importance of the service sector in providing employment and promoting exports.
questions.answer:
Employment: the service sector employed 29.4% of workers in 2009–10, and this share is rising. Educated people (graduates, engineers, doctors, professionals) find jobs in banking, IT, transport, education and health. It pays more than agriculture and offers year-round, non-seasonal work.
Exports: India's business services — IT, consultancy and legal services — are of world standard and earned about ₹4.35 lakh crore of foreign exchange in 2009–10. The sector also attracts foreign direct investment, which creates still more jobs.

questions.q: Explain the role of agriculture in the Indian economy.
questions.answer:
(1) National income: more than 50% at independence, about 15% in 2009–10.
(2) Employment: the mainstay of the economy. About 70% of people depended on it at independence and about 50% in 2009–10.
(3) Food: it feeds a large and growing population (234 million tonnes of food grains).
(4) Raw materials: it supplies the sugar, jute, cotton, vanaspati, paper and food-processing industries.
(5) Market: farmers buy industrial goods such as pumps, fertiliser and tractors.
